The linker error `undefined reference to '__device_dts_ord_39'` indicates that the device object for the `buttons` node (defined in `tests/drivers/input/gpio_keys/boards/native_sim.overlay`) was not generated. This typically happens when the corresponding device driver's source code is not compiled and linked into the final firmware.

The `gpio-keys` driver is defined by `compatible = "gpio-keys"`. Its Kconfig entry, `CONFIG_INPUT_GPIO_KEYS`, has a `depends on !DT_HAS_GPIO_KEYS_ENABLED && INPUT` clause.
In this test, `tests/drivers/input/gpio_keys/boards/native_sim.overlay` defines a `gpio-keys` node with `status = "okay"`, which causes `DT_HAS_GPIO_KEYS_ENABLED` to be set to `y`.
Due to the `!DT_HAS_GPIO_KEYS_ENABLED` dependency, `CONFIG_INPUT_GPIO_KEYS` will be `n`. When `CONFIG_INPUT_GPIO_KEYS` is `n`, the Zephyr build system will not include the `gpio_keys.c` driver source file (located at `drivers/input/gpio_keys/gpio_keys.c`) in the compilation.

To resolve this, the `gpio_keys.c` driver source file must be explicitly included in the test application's build. This can be achieved by adding it to the `target_sources` in the test's `CMakeLists.txt`.

target_sources(app PRIVATE ${app_sources})
========
